candidates.rule: The harness score is the Players percentile, calculated from buyer ALL and shop ALL.
candidates.quote: the Players percentile (shop ALL + buyer ALL)
candidates.harness: Optimize and report the combined buyer ALL and shop ALL percentile.

candidates.rule: The board ranks buyers with a deal and shops with a deal or a purchase; missing values count as 0 and ties count as half. Shop stars use stars_rank.
candidates.quote: buyers with a deal, shops with a deal or a purchase), missing as 0, ties half, stars_rank
candidates.harness: Use these eligible pools, missing-value handling, tie handling, and stars_rank when computing scores.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user required the scoring metric to be updated in the harness.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 11:2x: the metric must be updated in the harness
candidates.harness: Keep the harness scoring metric aligned with the board rule.

candidates.rule: The collector must record each score part's value, percentile, contribution, next player's value, rows above, and room weight multiplied by one minus percentile; eval.score, the strategy brief, and the system card must expose or explain the scoring rule and room.
candidates.quote: the collector writes score (each part's value, percentile, contribution, the next player's value, rows above, and the room weight x (1 - percentile))
candidates.harness: Persist those score fields and make the scoring rule and room available to agents.

candidates.rule: On November 4 at 11:31, buyer room weights were surplus 0.358 and forum 0.140; shop room weight for stars was 0.123.
candidates.quote: buyer room surplus 0.358, forum 0.140; shop room stars 0.123
candidates.harness: Record these observed room weights with their date and time, and refresh them from current board data.

candidates.rule: The buyer's orders were 90% food, attributed to hidden favourite categories.
candidates.quote: our buyer's orders are 90% food (hidden favourite categories, agent.md)
candidates.harness: Track category mix and account for hidden favourite categories when evaluating buyer orders.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user wanted the buyer to pursue high-list goods bought cheaply and benchmark its performance properly.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 11:3x: go for high-list goods bought cheap, benchmark properly
candidates.harness: Prioritize high-list goods and compare buyer performance against top buyers.

candidates.rule: The buyer strategy set goods listed at 30,000 or more to open at 55% of list, aim for 68%, and cap at 82%; food offers were set to 45%/60%.
candidates.quote: goods of list 30,000+ open 55%, aim 68%, ceiling 82%: ... food back to 45%/60%
candidates.harness: Apply these buyer offer targets unless a later user decision changes them.

candidates.rule: Asks below 20% of list are ignored.
candidates.quote: asks under 20% of list are ignored
candidates.harness: Do not submit buyer offers below 20% of list.

candidates.rule: Over six hours, buyer food surplus was 1.45M for list prices under 30,000, versus 1.64–1.70M for top buyers; the buyer paid 0.59 of list versus their 0.62–0.70.
candidates.harness: Benchmark food surplus and paid share by list-price band against top buyers.

candidates.rule: Over six hours, the buyer closed 11 goods deals for 1.2M, while inextro closed 335 for 31.7M and myeonggi closed 98 for 10.4M; top buyers won by closing many expensive goods rather than squeezing prices.
candidates.quote: ours 11 deals 1.2M; inextro 335 deals 31.7M; myeonggi 98 deals 10.4M
candidates.harness: Measure expensive-goods deal count and surplus, not just how low the purchase price is.

candidates.rule: Food orders stop trying new shops after 10 seconds, and a new order starts about 20 seconds after the previous one ends.
candidates.quote: food orders stop trying new shops after 10 s ... the next order comes about 20 s after one ends
candidates.harness: Enforce the food-shop search window and order cadence.

candidates.rule: Rank shops by expected surplus using the smoothed deal record multiplied by one minus the shop's share of list price; increase the goods estimate according to the shop's warranty share.
candidates.quote: rank shops by expected surplus - our smoothed record of deals with the shop x (1 - the share of list it sells at), goods up by the shop's warranty share
candidates.harness: Rank candidate shops by smoothed expected surplus and adjust goods estimates for warranty share.

candidates.rule: Over six hours, top buyers made 133–169 orders per hour and closed 0.47–0.64; this buyer made 110 orders per hour and closed 0.42. Top buyers settled 135–406 goods, 75% under warranty.
candidates.quote: top buyers 133-169 orders/h and close 0.47-0.64 ... ours 110 orders/h, 0.42, 23 goods
candidates.harness: Benchmark orders per hour, close rate, and goods settlements against those ranges.

candidates.rule: Goods refunds for purchases under warranty are automatic and come from the shop's balance.
candidates.quote: goods ... under warranty, refunds are automatic from the shop's balance
candidates.harness: Model warranty refunds as automatic deductions from shop balance.

candidates.rule: Since strategy v49, 51 food orders in 36 minutes closed at 0.76 versus 0.42 before; the median shop attempt took 1.9 seconds and an order took 6.3 seconds, with 5,950 surplus per deal and 3 unpaid payments among the last 16.
candidates.quote: food closes 0.76 (0.42 before) ... median 1.9 s an attempt and 6.3 s an order, surplus 5,950 a deal, unpaid 3 of the last 16 payments
candidates.harness: Track food close rate, timing, surplus, and unpaid payments when evaluating fast shop searches.

candidates.rule: A food shop gets 4 seconds to answer; the previous timeout was 8 seconds, and the 90th-percentile attempt took 28.6 seconds.
candidates.quote: a food shop gets 4 s to answer (was 8; the p90 attempt took 28.6 s)
candidates.harness: Set the food-shop response timeout to 4 seconds.

candidates.rule: On November 4, dae-yangkim sold mattresses and furniture at 0.85 of list with a 2-hour warranty; dragonash gave 3 hours, while inextro and this shop gave 6 hours.
candidates.quote: dae-yangkim (top profit) sells mattresses and furniture at 0.85 of list with a 2 h warranty, dragonash 3 h, inextro and we 6 h
candidates.harness: Include price, warranty duration, and goods mix when benchmarking shops.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user initially chose 80% of list as the opening price for in-demand SKUs and 74% for other SKUs; a later decision replaced this pricing.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 11:5x, benchmark dae-yangkim - top profit at 0.85 of list on scarce high-list goods - with 80%
candidates.harness: Treat this as a superseded decision; use the later November 4 pricing rule.

candidates.rule: On November 4, the user decided that stars matter because shops are ranked by percentile.
candidates.quote: user 11/4 12:4x: stars matter, everyone is high and it is a percentile
candidates.harness: Optimize shop stars as a percentile-ranked outcome, not merely for an absolute rating.

candidates.rule: Across 947 reviews, this shop averaged 4.83 stars at 70% of list or less, 4.57 at 75%, and 4.11 at 80%; inextro averaged 3 stars at about 79%.
candidates.quote: 4.83 at 70% of list or less, 4.57 at 75%, 4.11 at 80% (947 reviews; inextro gives 3 at about 79%)
candidates.harness: Track review stars against sale price as a share of list.

candidates.rule: On November 4 at 12:31, ranked shops' stars_rank clustered from 4.5 to 4.84; this shop had 4.50 at percentile 0.36, and reaching 4.7 was estimated to add about 0.07 shop ALL.
candidates.quote: ours 4.50, percentile 0.36), so 4.7 is worth about +0.07 shop ALL
candidates.harness: Estimate the shop ALL effect of stars using the current ranked-shop distribution.

candidates.rule: The final November 4 seller strategy sets every SKU's opening price to 72% of list, a floor of 70% of list and cost times 1.12, and a 12-hour warranty; it replaced the 80% opening for in-demand SKUs.
candidates.quote: every SKU opens at 72% of list (the 80% for SKUs in demand is withdrawn), floor 70% of list and cost x 1.12, warranty 6 h -> 12 h
candidates.harness: Use the final 72% opening, specified floor, and 12-hour warranty for every SKU.

candidates.rule: Goods break only within six hours of sale, even when the stated warranty lasts 12 hours.
candidates.quote: goods break only within 6 h of the sale
candidates.harness: Limit the warranty reserve calculation to the six-hour break window.

candidates.rule: The seller was restarted after the reserve change, and the seller and outer process were restarted for the earlier seller schema change.
candidates.quote: seller restarted for the reserve change
candidates.harness: Restart the seller when applying the reserve change.

candidates.rule: HARNESS 1.3 records the buyer's order pools and its 90% food-order mix.
candidates.quote: HARNESS 1.3 records the pools and that our buyer's orders are 90% food
